lines.en: As I slowly reached out, my thumb touched the cold screen.
At that moment, something like sparks rippled across it.
[The file has been updated to a new version.]
―Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World(Final Revision).TXT
In that brief interval, the filename had changed.
······Final Revision?
Almost unconsciously, I scrolled through the file.
But why? The scroll bar was almost at the very bottom of the file. A file that felt as though someone had just finished editing it. Without thinking, I scrolled farther down.
Had the ‘epilogue’ of Ways of Survival, the one I had never seen, been added?
The file, continuing beyond the point where the main story ended. It was a story I had never seen before.
Without thinking, I read it aloud.
Every round reaches its ending in its own way.
The 1863rd round was no different.
[You have cleared every scenario in the 〈Star Stream〉.]
She had done it. Countless sentences flashing through her mind the moment she saw the message.
The fallen ‘Dokkaebi King’ before her, and the companions of the 1863rd round she had led here.
“Boss! We won!”
Kim Namwoon, bawling his eyes out. Watching Lee Hyunsung approach to support her, Han Sooyoung realized that she had done it.
「This was the end of the 1863rd round.」
It had been a long fight.
From being suddenly summoned from the third round into the 1863rd to reaching an ending of her own in this world······.
She had nearly given up several times along the way. What had kept her from giving up to the very end were the words ‘that guy’ had left her then.
「“Moving on to the next scenario is better than sleeping forever.”」
The guy who had come from the same third round as her.
The man who wore the same coat and used the same weapon.
「“It's not all over just because the Apocalypse Dragon has been released. You know that, don't you?”」
The guy who had ruined her plan, released the Apocalypse Dragon, and finally even made Yoo Joonghyuk leave the scenarios.
Even now, when she closed her eyes, she could see that moment vividly. A single ‘character’ breaking free of his own story and finding freedom······.
“Boss, we did it. We did it!”
Putting out her cigarette, Han Sooyoung spoke to Lee Hyunsung, who could barely contain his joy.
“Help the kids up and head back.”
“What about you, Boss······?”
“I'm going to have one more smoke. Go on ahead.”
“······I can't do that!”
······For such a slow-witted guy, he picked up on things awfully fast.
Han Sooyoung signaled to the archangel beside Lee Hyunsung with a glance.
“Jophiel.”
Commander of the Red Cosmos, Jophiel.
The archangel who had crossed into this worldline with that guy from the third round.
[Let's go, big guy.]
“No, Boss-nim!”

Watching the archangel return to Earth with the companions, Han Sooyoung took out her last cigarette. The companions of ‘Ways of Survival’ grew distant. As she watched them weeping, filled with the satisfaction of having cleared every scenario, she gave a bitter smile.
Flying away with her wings spread, Jophiel looked back at her.
―Do you intend to go alone?
Instead of answering, Han Sooyoung waved the glowing tip of her cigarette.
Once all her companions had disappeared, Han Sooyoung slowly turned around.
「Final Wall.」
The wall that barred the ending of this worldline, and the wall that recorded everything in the universe.

Han Sooyoung knew this wall existed. She even knew how to open it. There were things she had glimpsed while connected to the Han Sooyoung of the third round, and above all, the information she had obtained through Kim Dokja when he visited this round had been decisive.
[‘Wall that Decides Samsara’ has returned to its place.]
One by one, Han Sooyoung began fitting in the [Walls] she had gathered beforehand.
[‘Wall that Divides Good and Evil’ has returned to its place.]
[‘Wall of Impossible Communication’ has returned to its place.]
But one fragment was still missing.
The fragment that only one guy across all universes possessed, [Fourth Wall].
Han Sooyoung gazed down at her hand, then slowly brought it to the groove in the wall.
[The Story ‘Predictive Plagiarism’ begins its story.]
She did not have that [Wall].
But couldn't she at least make a similar fragment?
[The Story ‘Ultimate Lie’ begins its story!]
Han Sooyoung began wringing out every Story she could imagine.
Once, just once, she had seen the true form of [Fourth Wall]. When she had used [Eyes of Truth] and been blocked by [Fourth Wall], she had certainly seen part of that wall.
[The Story ‘Predictive Plagiarism’ activates at full capacity!]
Han Sooyoung's rapidly moving fingers began writing a Story. The Story of the wall as she imagined it. The single story that would make up that wall.
Bzzzzzzzt······!
「“I'm Dokja.”」
「Kim Dokja (金獨子). My father gave me that name so I would become a man who was strong even on his own.」
The next moment, Han Sooyoung's fingertips slipped straight into the wall.
Then her arm, her shoulder, her head and torso······ and finally, all of her seeped into the wall.
[The system of ‘Final Wall’ is astonished by your Story information······.]
[A temporary system error has occurred!]
Holding back the urge to vomit, Han Sooyoung felt around on the floor.
She had succeeded.
She had made it safely inside this damned wall.
When she raised her head, the first thing she saw was a small room. Inside were bundles packed full of belongings and a few small video panels.
She knew the Story playing on the panels.
「The constellation ‘Demon King of Salvation’ has reached his ■■.」
「The ■■ of ‘Demon King of Salvation’ is ‘Eternity.’」
The ending of the third round. That guy, too, had carried out the scenarios to the end in his own worldline. And so, at last, he had chosen to become this world's only reader.
「“In a world without scenarios, with nothing left but the desire to see the next story…… some baby with a truly horrifying imagination.”」
He would keep growing smaller, until one day he became this world's unconscious. And so he would continue an endless story.
The Han Sooyoung of the 1863rd round knew this. If asked how she knew, she simply knew.
‘I'd have ended it that way too.’
This world—a world for stories.
Yoo Joonghyuk's story and Kim Dokja's story were, in the end, merely stories moving toward a single completion.
Han Sooyoung watched the subway recede on the screen. For a long time, she watched this universe's god travel toward a world no one would know or remember.
And a few paces ahead of her, someone was watching the screen, dabbing away tears with a handkerchief.
[Eek?]
“Are you the real ‘Dokkaebi King’?”
[······How on earth did you get in here?]
The Dokkaebi King they had certainly killed was standing before her, perfectly fine.
Drawing [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] from inside her coat, Han Sooyoung asked,
“I thought you were too weak. Why didn't you fight properly? What are you doing here?”
[Whoa, wait. The scenarios are over. I have no wish to fight you.]
She really could sense no will to fight from the Dokkaebi King as he waved both hands.
The Dokkaebi King's eyes gleamed as he watched the faint sparks leaping from Han Sooyoung's body. His gaze was fixed on the malfunctioning [Final Wall].
[You copied ‘Final Wall’······? How could such an astonishing talent······ Who on earth are you? Your soul is······ like the very sum of all talent.]
“What were you thinking, putting up a scarecrow like that? Are you looking down on this worldline?”
[Heh, looking down on it? Every worldline's story is precious. It's just······ this worldline no longer has much meaning. The most important Story has just ended.]
As he spoke, the Dokkaebi King turned back to the panel.
When Han Sooyoung quietly stirred her Stories, the Dokkaebi King gave a sly smile.
[Why are you getting so angry? Your stories ended safely, didn't they?]
“Don't touch this worldline's ending.”
The moment she said that, an image of the 1863rd round appeared on the panel.
Lee Hyunsung and Kim Namwoon supporting each other. A wide shot showed the companions' retreating backs.
[Ah, of course. It's not an important worldline anyway······.]
Watching the Dokkaebi King shrug indifferently, Han Sooyoung felt an inexplicable emptiness.
Was this how this round's story would end?
Was it really all right for it to end like this?
[And above all······ the new ‘Oldest Dream’ would not wish to see such a thing.]
At that, Han Sooyoung looked up into the air without realizing it.
‘Oldest Dream.’
The Kim Dokja she had known had become such a being.
Which meant he might be watching this scene now.
[Do you think he'll answer just because you look up like that? There were people who believed in gods in your world too. Did those gods answer every single time a human called?]
“That's different.”
[Well······ think what you like. Anyway, I'm about to make my ‘escape.’ May I go?]
“Where are you going?”
[This worldline's story is over, so I should go somewhere else. I've worked hard all this time, and there's a place I've always wanted to visit······.]
“So you're running off after tossing together those half-assed scenarios?”
[Why weren't you born into a worldline with a conscientious Dokkaebi King?]
Frowning, Han Sooyoung released another wave of energy.
“After everything it took to get here······ shouldn't you at least give me a reward for clearing the scenarios?”
The ‘Dokkaebi King’ sighed.
[Well, all right. I can grant you one wish.]
“······I want to see him.”
For a moment, Han Sooyoung couldn't understand why she had said that.
「“Because you're there, too.”」
「“I trusted the you in the third round.”」
She couldn't quite understand this stifled feeling.
But if she saw him again, she felt she could find out what it was.
The Dokkaebi King tilted his head.
[By him, you mean······.]
When Han Sooyoung gestured toward the screen with her chin, the Dokkaebi King cried out in horror.
[Are your eyes screwed on wrong? He is no longer a being I can meet.]
“He can be from another worldline. He doesn't have to be one who's seen the end.”
Kim Dokja was no longer visible on the screen.
“I just want to see him one more time.”
[There is only one of him in this universe.]
If the Dokkaebi King was being this firm, it really must be impossible.
Looking at the dejected Han Sooyoung, the Dokkaebi King spoke with a crafty expression.
[······Well, there is one way I could grant your wish.]
“What?”
[It's a worldline that's normally off limits, but I memorized its entry coordinates when the new ‘Oldest Dream’ ascended. ······However, the ‘Oldest Dream’ there will not recognize you.]
Han Sooyoung brightened and asked,
“Where is it?”
[It's the place I was planning to visit. Once this universe's epic ended, I wanted to go there first.]
As he spoke, the Dokkaebi King stretched both hands high into the sky. The lofty universe of the 〈Star Stream〉 spread out there.
Looking up at that sight with a solemn expression, the Dokkaebi King spoke.

[Aren't you curious? Where this universe began. Who built this intricate galaxy of Stories. Who created ‘scenarios’ in this world. Just who completed this world of contradictions, where effects make causes, and causes bring forth effects!]
Han Sooyoung realized what the Dokkaebi King was after.
He meant to go to the worldline where this universe began.
「The place where ‘Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World’ began.」
「The universe where tls123 was.」
[I am going to meet my god. If you wish, I will let you come along!]
Bzzzzzzzzt!
With a thunderous roar, a backlash of probability began raging between her and the Dokkaebi King. Amid pain that seemed to tear her entire soul to pieces, she briefly saw the Dokkaebi King smile.
[Let us survive and meet again.]
That was the last thing Han Sooyoung remembered of the 1863rd round.
When she sat bolt upright with a gasp, it was two in the morning. Her back was soaked with sweat. The ticking of the clock's second hand.
······Was it a dream?

Han Sooyoung got up groggily. The feel of soft covers wrapped around her arms and legs. For some reason, the bed felt unfamiliar. She drank the water left on the bedside table, went into the adjoining bathroom, and switched on the light. As the orange incandescent bulb lit the darkness, she saw herself in the mirror.
A bob that reached her shoulders. A beauty mark beneath her eye, all the more conspicuous when she narrowed her eyes. It was unmistakably her face. Her own, and yet.
“······What is this?”
Suddenly, her chest felt tight.
[You have entered the ‘first worldline.’]

Plastic models and comics displayed on the dressing table. Han Sooyoung rushed out of the bathroom. A familiar-looking schoolbag beside the bed. The darkness in the house no longer felt unfamiliar. She opened the bag with trembling hands and found textbooks inside. Neat handwriting marked them.
―Grade 6, Class 2, No. 2, Han Sooyoung.
Han Sooyoung was now thirteen.
Suddenly, she was a sixth-grader. Why on earth?
All through the early morning, Han Sooyoung was in a daze.
At first, she wondered if she had regressed, like Yoo Joonghyuk.
[Your free activity time has ended.]
[Your next free activity period is scheduled to begin in approximately 14 hours.]
[Control of the body will be reclaimed.]
But when that message appeared and she lost control of her body, she realized what had happened to her.
[You may exercise control only while the original body's ego is asleep.]
She had possessed her own childhood self.
‘······Could this be a new scenario?’
But however long she waited, no scenario messages appeared.
She watched her younger self wash her sleepy face, eat, and go to school. There was nothing else she could do.
And exactly fourteen hours later, the following messages appeared.
[The original body's ego has fallen asleep.]
[Your free activity time begins.]
[Control of the body is being transferred to you.]
By day, she could only watch her clueless thirteen-year-old self go about her life. At night, control of the body returned with uncanny regularity. And then she would cry out,
“······What the hell am I supposed to do?”
Her thoughts were a tangle. If this really was the ‘first worldline,’ her actions now might affect every worldline that would arise.
Taking a deep breath, Han Sooyoung decided to assess her surroundings first.
Three rooms and a living room, furnished with expensive, simple furniture.
Han Sooyoung knew this home.
A housekeeper who came to work early in the morning. A lazy bodyguard who occasionally checked who came and went. And parents who took turns visiting each weekend in unfamiliar cars.
A National Assembly member for a father and an actress for a mother.
Han Sooyoung had never once thought of them as family.
The world did not know she existed.
And her parents would not want her existence revealed, either.
“······It really is all the same.”

Han Sooyoung flipped through the books piled high on her thirteen-year-old self's desk. Some were books she had loved; others she barely remembered. Her other self probably held those faint memories. In any case, the wear on them made it clear she had read them all.
「Everyone has a life of their own.」
Seeing that she had even underlined such a trite sentence gave her goosebumps.
Sentences as unremarkable as this must have piled up to make the person called Han Sooyoung.
That was when the doorbell rang.
······At this hour?

She immediately pressed the button to check the entrance. At first, she thought it was the bodyguard, but a closer look at the screen showed that the bodyguard was unconscious. A middle-aged man in a fedora smiled and waved at her.
―It's the Dokkaebi King.
“Why do you look like that?”
“I suddenly became human when I came here. Most of my system authority was confiscated, too······ Why did you get younger?”
“You made me this way.”
“I did no such thing. It was the influence of profound probability······ Well, anyway, I'll come in for a moment.”
With a sigh, Han Sooyoung led the Dokkaebi King inside.
“Do you live alone?”
“Yeah.”
“You have plenty of spare rooms.”
“······I'm telling you now, don't expect me to put you up.”
The Dokkaebi King looked crestfallen. Han Sooyoung made tea with a tea bag, brought it out, and asked,
“So why did you bring me to this worldline?”
“Now we look for the ‘creator’ together.”
“How?”
“We'll have to think about that.”
“You came without preparing anything?”
“I do have some ideas, of course. That novel, for instance.”
Han Sooyoung's expression stiffened.
It seemed the Dokkaebi King knew ‘Ways of Survival’ existed after all.
“The person who wrote that novel is probably the ‘god’ who designed this universe.”
tls123.
The author of ‘Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World.’
With a soft sigh, Han Sooyoung fetched her laptop.
“I already looked.”
―No search results.
“That novel hasn't been uploaded yet.”
“······Hmm, has something gone wrong?”
“We must have come too early. I'm sure it starts being serialized this year.”
“How do you know?”
“If what I heard was right, Kim Dokja first read this novel when he was fifteen. I'm thirteen, so he must be fifteen now.”
Han Sooyoung recalled the crumpled little notebook Kim Dokja had once given her. That guy, who had written down all sorts of information before leaving—perhaps in a hurry.
“His fifteen-year-old self······ How adorable······.”
“There's something else I want to know.”
“What is it?”
“What happens if ‘Ways of Survival’ never appears in this world?”
“Pardon?”
The Dokkaebi King hesitated at the question, then continued.
“Hmm······ then he would not be able to read the novel.”
“And since he can't read it, does that naturally mean ‘Ways of Survival’ won't become reality?”
“······That could be so. At least the worldlines that branch from here might never undergo the ‘apocalypse.’”
If that was true, if she could prevent Kim Dokja from reading ‘Ways of Survival,’ she might be able to prevent this worldline's destruction.
“I think I understand what you're thinking. You mean to stop ‘Ways of Survival’ from being serialized, don't you?”
“That's right.”
Han Sooyoung nodded. At least if tls123 wasn't an inhuman being, she might be able to stop this worldline's destruction herself.
Then the Dokkaebi King objected.
“An interesting idea. But you don't even know who the author is······.”
“Have you ever read that novel?”
“No, I haven't. Have you?”
“Yeah.”
Han Sooyoung thought for a moment, then continued.
“That novel is terribly written.”
“It's full of exposition from the start, it has no sense of how much space to give anything, and it shows no consideration for the reader at all. Only Kim Dokja read it from beginning to end.”
“Oh, how truly remarkable······.”
“Do you think that makes sense?”
The Dokkaebi King narrowed his eyes as though asking what she meant. Han Sooyoung continued.

“Every author rereads their own novel. Besides, with webnovels, you can't revise everything perfectly, so they would have clicked their own posts again and again, even just to fix typos. But······ after chapter one hundred, every chapter had a view count of one.”
Only then did the Dokkaebi King's eyes widen, as though he understood.
“You don't mean······.”
“That's right. I think he's the ‘author’ of Ways of Survival. I don't know why he wrote it and then denied it, but I'm sure of it.”
A blank Hangul word processor window open on her laptop, as always. Watching the blinking cursor, Han Sooyoung spoke.
“Find Kim Dokja. Before he starts that damned ‘Ways of Survival.’”
The problem was how to find this ‘Kim Dokja.’
“Don't you know where he lives? Without system authority, we have to find him ourselves.”
“Somewhere in Seoul, probably.”
“······Are there any other distinguishing features?
“Well, he'll be hiding somewhere, absorbed in reading fantasy novels······.”
“How on earth am I supposed to find him with that?”
“Hell if I know. That's for you to figure out. I'm only an elementary schooler.”
With those words, Han Sooyoung promptly passed out. When she woke again, the Dokkaebi King was nowhere to be seen.
“······So that's why I always dozed off at school.”
No wonder she had been so sleepy whenever she went to school······ Had another ego been waking up and moving around?
Waiting for the Dokkaebi King was rather boring, so Han Sooyoung did what she could in the spare hours before dawn.
Mostly, she browsed blogs.
“I bet that guy had a blog······.”

When she grew bored, she would make a secret folder on her laptop and write a little fiction. Mostly brief pieces to keep her hand in. But the day after she finished one of those pieces, something very strange happened. Her thirteen-year-old daytime self went and did something.
“Sooyoung, when did you get so good at writing?”
She won the grand prize at a suddenly announced school writing contest.
What was more, the piece was exactly the same as the one she had scribbled down before dawn.
“It just suddenly came pouring out.”
Thinking back, she had started hearing that she was a good writer when she was thirteen. From this point onward, Han Sooyoung would begin pursuing writing in earnest.
A month passed like that, then two.
Han Sooyoung began to enjoy living as an observer of her thirteen-year-old self.
The fifteen-year-old Kim Dokja was probably living somewhere in this world, too.
Thinking about that made Han Sooyoung feel strangely happy.
What should she say first when she met that annoying bastard?
Time passed swiftly. September came, then October.
Occasionally, her parents came home and left presents she didn't even like.
And finally, December. Little by little, Han Sooyoung began feeling that something was wrong.
―No search results.
Why had tls123 still not begun the serial? Had she done something wrong and changed the future?
But that couldn't be. She hadn't even met Kim Dokja yet.
······What would happen if ‘Ways of Survival’ didn't begin this year?
Would this world continue to exist without ‘Ways of Survival’?
Perhaps that wouldn't be such a bad world.
Without ‘Ways of Survival,’ the world would never have to meet its end. Then······.
That was when the telephone rang.
The moment she answered, assuming it must be her parents again.
―I've found him.
“What? Where? No, where are you now?”
Her heart began to race.
They had found Kim Dokja. At last.
But what she heard next was something not even [Predictive Plagiarism] could have predicted.
―This place is, well······ what they call a hospital emergency room.

Evading her bodyguard, Han Sooyoung took a taxi before dawn. The hospital wasn't far away. Doctors and nurses hurried to and fro even at this hour. Patients' screams sounded intermittently. The deep-rooted smell of death lingered on empty gurneys.
Even where there were no scenarios, someone was always dying.
Tiny apocalypses. A place where unrecorded lives faded away.
Half out of her mind, Han Sooyoung searched the gurneys.
“Ah―”
There lay fifteen-year-old Kim Dokja. His face was pale and haggard. An IV needle was inserted into the boy's bandaged wrist.
“No, I'm telling you, it wasn't our fault! The kid, at school―”
Faces that didn't resemble Kim Dokja's. A couple who seemed to be relatives of his—cousins, perhaps—were shouting irritably at a doctor. Looking their way, Han Sooyoung demanded of the Dokkaebi King,
“What happened to him?”
“They say he jumped from a classroom window.”
Han Sooyoung slowly reached out and examined Kim Dokja's body. A body wrapped in crude casts and bandages. Deep bruises on his face. An arm without a trace of muscle lay limply at his side.
Han Sooyoung took the boy's hand.
It was as small as her own.
“Do something······ Please, do something.”
“Don't worry. His injuries aren't fatal. Fortunately, it was a low floor, and he hit a tree······.”
“That's not what I mean!”
She saw the couple approaching from a distance. The couple shouting something, perhaps having spotted Han Sooyoung.
But Han Sooyoung couldn't hear their voices.
Why on earth?
「“If it hadn't been for that novel, I probably would've died back then.”」
She couldn't tell whether it was her own memory or one from the third round.
「“There you go exaggerating again.”」
「“I'm serious.”」

Amid a distant ringing in her ears, old memories washed over her. Leaning on the Dokkaebi King, she left the hospital. She could see medical staff and paramedics wheeling a new patient into the emergency room.
“At least we found him.”
“He truly lives up to his reputation in person. Did you feel the terrifying energy coming from his entire body? Now, if he would only open his own world―”
As though looking forward to the apocalypse that would soon visit this worldline, the Dokkaebi King chattered on. Han Sooyoung staggered and murmured,
“Kim Dokja said he read that novel when he was fifteen.”
“Yes, so soon―”
“If he can't read that novel······ what will happen to him?”
“Pardon?”
If ‘Ways of Survival’ never began, the world would not end.
But what would happen to Kim Dokja?
“Hello?”
“Are you crying?”

Kim Dokja's tragedy was a common one. Something that might have been overcome if a few small glances of concern, a little goodwill, had come together. But this was no situation in which she could expect that concern, that goodwill.
Who on earth could a thirteen-year-old elementary schooler save when she could barely regain her senses, and only before dawn?
“Why?”
Even so, she couldn't leave it to that Dokkaebi King.
His way of speaking was strange, he couldn't use the system, and he was an unemployed dokkaebi with no one to vouch for his identity. How could she trust him······?
Han Sooyoung stared blankly down at her hands.
「“That novel saved me. So I have to repay the protagonist.”」
Something that could save Kim Dokja.
“Do you have any money?”
“Pardon?”
“Give me five thousand won. No, ten thousand.”
Han Sooyoung immediately snatched the Dokkaebi King's money and ran to a nearby internet café.
The Dokkaebi King chased after her, wailing.
“That's all the money I have!”

Unnoticed by the dozing internet café owner, Han Sooyoung picked up a pay-later card, logged in, and opened a browser. She entered the address of the webnovel platform she always visited and searched for the author's name.
―No search results.
tls123 had still not appeared.
Although the last day of the year was already approaching, the serial had not begun.
Han Sooyoung stared at the screen for a while, then pressed the platform's [Sign Up] button.
She didn't know who tls123 was. But at least, if tls123 wasn't Kim Dokja. If someone else had written that damned novel, whoever they were. Then.
―No one is using this username. Would you like to use it?
Perhaps it didn't matter who that person was.
Her hand trembled on the mouse.
The button of tragedy lay beneath her fingertip. If she pressed this button······ the destruction of countless worldlines would begin.
But if she didn't press it.
―Yes.
The ‘little world’ she had seen would disappear.
―Congratulations on joining, tls123-nim!
Han Sooyoung checked the time.
[You have 3 hours of free activity time remaining.]
[When the original body wakes, your control will be forcibly reclaimed.]

Opening a Hangul window, she immediately began typing. Her fingers flew as though she were pouring out a manuscript she had long been composing in her mind. Typing without a single typo. Sentences so intricate it was as though an entire world had been carved out intact. Yet the narration offered no structure designed with the reader in mind, no devices to draw them in. She wrote and wrote that dull story.
Just one person, at least.
Hoping that they would, without fail, read this story.
「This is a lie.」
Countless worlds perished beneath her fingertips.
Countless characters died.
「At least, until it becomes the truth.」
Every possibility she could gauge through [Predictive Plagiarism] flooded her mind.
Some became narrative, and some became setting.
How much time passed? At last, Han Sooyoung's fingers stopped.
「Facing the unfathomable disaster that had descended on him, Yoo Joonghyuk said,」
[Predictive Plagiarism] could not reveal every story.
「“I will never give up until I see the end of the scenarios. So―”」

She didn't know whether Yoo Joonghyuk had really said those words. Because all of this was a fictional story. Because she had made it up. And so she wanted to write those words. To borrow Yoo Joonghyuk's voice and write those words.
「“Don't you give up, either.”」
Breathing deeply, Han Sooyoung slowly raised her head. When she turned, the Dokkaebi King was gazing at the screen with an ecstatic expression.
“Dokkaebi King.”
The Dokkaebi King slowly sank to his knees and waited for her words.
“······I'm going to sleep.”
[You have expended far too much mental strength in a short time!]
[Your ego is becoming subconscious······.]
When she regained consciousness, she was in bed.
Midnight. An entire day's cycle must have passed while she was unconscious.
······Damn it, what have I done?
Clutching her head, Han Sooyoung got up. On the desk, her laptop's bright blue desktop was visible. Without thinking, she opened a browser and visited the serialization platform.
There were already several comments on what she had posted before dawn yesterday.
Most were nasty comments calling it boring, an exposition dump, and the like.
“Of course it is. I wrote it in a rush in just two hours······ And I did it to make it as much like ‘Ways of Survival’ as possible, okay?”
Among those comments, one stood out.
―Author-nim. This is really interesting. How often do you post chapters?
An almost absurd innocence, using his own name as his username. Han Sooyoung stared at that name for a long time. Looking closer, she saw one more comment.
―Will you... post tomorrow too?
Han Sooyoung clenched and unclenched her fists again and again. Sweat dampened her little hands. Is it all right for me to write this?
Would it really be all right?
After hesitating for a long time, Han Sooyoung wrote a reply.
Thinking of someone who would still be alive beyond this monitor.
